25. Explain specifically how you believe: Beginning January 2025, my supervisor, Michael Thompson, repeatedly assigned me heavy lifting duties despite my documented physical restriction (chronic lower back pain) and without offering reasonable accommodations. On 01-15-2025 I raised concerns with Mr. Thompson about a pattern of heavier assignments being given to Hispanic employees; he responded with dismissive remarks referencing my marital status. On 02-10-2025 I contacted EEO Counselor Maria Gonzalez and initiated protected activity by reporting these assignments and the discriminatory pattern. Following that, on 02-18-2025 Mr. Thompson issued me a formal reprimand for alleged performance issues that were not applied to similarly situated non-Hispanic employees; the reprimand referenced incidents that other employees had engaged in without corrective action. Names of relevant individuals: Supervisor Michael Thompson (direct supervisor), HR representative Linda Perez (handled the reprimand documentation), coworkers Sara Lee and Robert Chang (observed differential treatment), and EEO Counselor Maria Gonzalez (EEO contact). I believe the adverse actions (assignment of heavy duties, failure to accommodate, and issuance of reprimand) were motivated by my race/national origin (Hispanic), my age (49), my sex (male), and in retaliation for engaging in protected EEO activity.
26. What remedies are you seeking to res: Requested remedies: 1) Removal of the disciplinary reprimand from my personnel record; 2) Retroactive back pay for lost shift differentials and overtime from date of adverse action (02-18-2025) through resolution if applicable; 3) Reasonable accommodation for my documented physical condition (lifting restrictions and reassignment of heavy lifting duties); 4) Training for supervisory staff on EEO, disability accommodation, and anti-retaliation; 5) A formal apology from my supervisor and a review of assignment practices to ensure nondiscriminatory treatment; 6) Monitoring to ensure no further retaliation.
